text:
The stock rose 0.83% today to $150.29, continuing a strong two-week rally up 6%. The move reflects oil prices settling after recent volatility—U.S. crude fell today as news of renewed U.S.-Iran peace efforts eased immediate supply-disruption fears that had pushed prices higher earlier in the week. ConocoPhillips, as a major oil producer, benefits when crude prices stay elevated; the current $103/barrel U.S. price and $123/barrel globally remain well above the lows earlier this month, supporting the company's cash flow and stock performance.

The broader context: oil markets have been swinging on Middle East geopolitical risk this week, with prices climbing Wednesday on conflict concerns, then moderating Thursday as diplomacy signals emerged. The company has now recovered most of the sharp 2.8% drop from Monday to Tuesday, suggesting investors view the current price level as stable enough to hold.
